newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russians in Svyazinvest group to improve telecoms.
newsitem.headline: Russians in Svyazinvest group to improve telecoms.

text.p: Russian members of the consortium which won a quarter stake in Svyazinvest said on Thursday they would work to improve the way the telecoms holding company was run.

A statement signed by Uneximbank president Vladimir Potanin and Svyazinvest general director Nail Ismailov said priority tasks included increasing the number of domestic telephone lines, implenting digital and non-cable technologies, auditing Svyazinvest subsidaries to international standards and simplifying internal accounting procedures.
"It (the company) will become more attractive for investors," the statement said.

The Svyazinvest auction, Russia's largest to date, has unleashed a public row between reformist ministers against influential newspapers and television stations controlled by Russian banks which made an unsuccessful bid.

The consortium which won was built around Uneximbank, Russia's third biggest bank, headed by Potanin, who was first deputy prime minister until March. It was backed by several foreign entities, including Deutsche Morgan Grenfell (DMG), billionaire financier George Soros and Morgan Stanley Asset Management.

Members of the losing consortium are Vladimir Gusinsky, founder of the Most financial and industrial group, and tycoon Boris Berezovsky, who has formally dropped his business roles to get a Kremlin post. They were joined by Spain's Telefonica .

The Uneximbank-led group offered $1.875 billion, against $1.71 offered by the other bidder. The size of the bids, far above the starting price of $1.18 billion, pleased analysts who had wanted to see Russia sell off a major company at a relatively fair market price.
